mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD spectra support random-coil structure in water and alpha-helical structure in DMPG micelles for selected peptides; NMR/HSQC supports SP1-1 micelle binding. This is membrane-association context, not proof of a killing pore by itself.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: SP1-1, SP8, SP10-10, SP13; SP1-1 NMR supplement

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=2:Figure 2; xml:sec=Membrane Activity of Selected Peptides; supp:pone.0071687.s002.pdf

mechanism_claims.limitations: Conformation in lipid mimetic systems is supportive mechanism context and is not treated as a standalone direct antimicrobial mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: DiSC3(5) membrane-potential assays directly show membrane depolarization differences: SP10-5 and SP13-2 caused significant membrane potential changes in C. michiganensis and P. syringae pv. syringae, SP1-1 was moderate, and SP10-2/SP8 were low or negative controls under the tested conditions.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: SP1-1, SP10-2, SP10-5, SP8, SP13-2 against C. michiganensis and P. syringae pv. syringae

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Membrane Activity of Selected Peptides; xml:fig=3:Figure 3

mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct evidence is membrane depolarization, not full molecular target resolution for every active peptide.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Plant-surface, apoplast-fluid, tomato-fruit, and fungal leaf assays support applied plant-protection activity for selected peptides while preserving that these assays are efficacy/context evidence rather than a separate molecular mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: SP1-1, SP10-2, SP10-5, SP10-D, SP13-D and comparator context in Table S5
